extracted.intended_audience: general news readers interested in fashion, race/ethnicity issues, and corporate public relations
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and observable actions for how a company should respond publicly after an offensive product or design prompts social-media backlash (apology, removal, commitments, engagement). Useful for evaluating corporate apologies and PR crisis responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate public apology
rubrics_metrics.description: Gucci said it "deeply apologizes for the offense caused by the wool balaclava jumper."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue a clear, direct apology acknowledging the offense. Use public channels (e.g., Twitter) so the apology is visible to those who complained. Avoid vague language that fails to acknowledge harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate product removal / discontinuation
rubrics_metrics.description: "We can confirm that the item has been immediately removed from our online store and all physical stores."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove the offending product from sale promptly and communicate that removal publicly. This is a concrete action that accompanies an apology and signals accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of values and commitment to internal change
rubrics_metrics.description: "We are fully committed to increasing diversity throughout our organization and turning this incident into a powerful learning moment for the Gucci team and beyond."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pair an apology with commitments to organizational change (e.g., increasing diversity, training, review processes). Frame the incident as a learning opportunity and specify intended steps where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid token apology + 'we did not know' pattern (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism that "Gigantic brands like @gucci create offensive 'fashion', quickly apologize, and then state, 'We did not know.' I don't care. This is unacceptable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely solely on a rapid, surface-level apology followed by claims of ignorance. Critics view repeated cycles of offensive product → quick apology → 'we didn't know' as insufficient; responses should include accountability and demonstrable changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity to timing and broader social context
rubrics_metrics.description: Users noted the controversy was taking place during Black History Month and expressed skepticism about the brand's response having real impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the timing and cultural context when responding; incidents coinciding with significant observances or heightened public attention demand extra sensitivity and substantive follow-through.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of social media reaction as an input and barometer
rubrics_metrics.description: The sweater "had been slammed on social media, with Twitter users saying it resembled blackface and expressing emotions ranging from exasperation to outrage."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor social-media responses closely; visible public outcry is a signal to act and shapes reputational consequences. Public perception should inform both the content and urgency of the response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with past precedent (withdraw offending items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference to Prada: the company "withdrew products after some items displayed in a Manhattan storefront were seen as depicting blackface imagery."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow precedents where brands withdrew items after similar controversies. Consistent corrective action across incidents builds credibility; failure to act consistently invites criticism and comparisons to past failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage affected communities and leaders when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Example of a political figure meeting Southern Christian Leadership Conference leaders "an effort to better understand how he can move past the scandal that has engulfed his office."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where relevant, engage with community leaders or representatives to understand impact and repair harm. Public meetings, outreach, or consultation can be part of remediation and rebuilding trust.
